category_title: Students without academic skill deficits who engage in active/disruptive work avoidance
minimal_context: Martin is participating in independent reading at his desk in a second-grade classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent reading. Please sit at your desk and read your book quietly.

STUDENT: (Turns his body away from the assigned materials and stares at the back of the classroom.)

TUTOR: Martin, you need to look at your book.

STUDENT: (Leans over to the next desk) Hey, what page are you on? Look at this.

TUTOR: Please stop talking and focus on your own reading.

STUDENT: (Gets out of his seat and walks away from his desk, leaving his book behind to avoid the reading task.)

options.A: Agree with the student that he is having a rough time with the reading task.
options.B: Make sure not to give the student attention during the independent reading activity.
options.C: Model the expected reading behavior for the student, telling him to do it the same as you.
options.D: Provide immediate instructional feedback, helping the student understand what he should have done.
